page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 60.0 GB of system memory. For acceleration, the instance includes a single NVIDIA P100 GPU based on the Pascal architecture, equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided via a bundled 472 GB SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. The host CPU exhibits weak multi-core and poor single-core performance, as evidenced by stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Memory bandwidth is average for small cached blocks but drops to weak for larger uncached blocks. However, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU delivers strong performance in specific workloads, achieving top-tier results in LLM inference prompt processing for both small and medium models, as well as top-tier text generation speeds for 7B parameter models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents an entry-level GPU option where the primary value lies in the bundled hardware accelerator and local SSD storage rather than raw CPU compute density. The trade-off involves lower CPU performance and moderate network throughput in exchange for dedicated GPU resources. This hardware profile is best suited for legacy GPU-accelerated workloads, small-to-medium LLM inference, basic machine learning model training, and applications that can leverage the local SSD for caching while offloading parallel tasks to the Pascal-based GPU.
